name: carry
description: Move this computer's settings to a backup, another computer, or the other disk. carry_fold saves a gzip backup of /home/bia under /home/bia/files. It includes settings, chats, passwords, Chrome, Telegram, the model, and MCP binaries for aarch64 and x86_64. It also lists each manually installed package with its version, architecture, and apt origin. The file is named name.unfold-<bytes>.tar.gz, where <bytes> is the unpacked size. carry_fold refuses when the disk has less free space than /home/bia. Ask the user and call carry_fold again with force=true only after they confirm. carry_unfold reads that backup, puts it on this computer, and reboots. MCP binaries already on this machine are kept; the archive only fills missing ones. An older backup whose name has no .unfold-<bytes> still unfolds after the user confirms: call carry_unfold again with force=true only after they confirm. Do the same when free space is below <bytes>. Do not pass force before they confirm. carry_discover lists computers that are waiting to receive a backup. carry_land makes this computer wait. Both screens show the same 6-digit code. Call carry_confirm only after the user says the codes match. Then this computer reboots with the other computer's settings. carry_fly sends this computer's backup to a waiting computer. If you leave host empty and only one computer is waiting, it sends there. carry_morph(disk=) folds an agent from that block device, then reboots. carry_update starts an attended OS update (or console /update) — not automatic at boot: from the attached flash stick or disk when there is one, else the newest bia release from GitHub over the internet (from='internet' forces that). It must be a higher version unless force=true. carry_rescue(disk=) from flash pushes this OS onto BIADISK for repair. carry_to_disk needs disk=/dev/sdX (or partition=); with Windows also pass partition or shrink_from+size_mib or size_mib. carry_to_flash needs disk= for the stick. Always choose devices with bash lsblk — there is no serial=internal/flash lookup. carry_to_disk then reboots into the disk (BootNext 'bia disk'); carry_to_flash then shut down. Do not expect boot to apply a newer flash by itself. A server on the internet that does not run bia yet (a VPS or rented server with Ubuntu or Debian that you reach over ssh) can become a land for this agent, prepared by you: 1) ask root first: it erases that server. Get its address and how to log in (an ssh key or password root gives you; never guess). 2) carry_new_land_secret(host=<address>): it is saved for that server, so you need not remember it. 3) bash: ssh root@<address> 'findmnt -no SOURCE /; lsblk -d -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE' to see the disk that holds / (e.g. /dev/vda or /dev/sda). 4) bash: ssh root@<address> "curl -fsSL https://github.com/zond80/bia/releases/latest/download/takeover.sh | bash -s -- --land --land-secret <secret> --yes --wipe <disk> --reboot" (use sudo bash when the login is not root). It checks RAM, disk and boot loader first and changes nothing if a check fails; read its output. Then the server reboots, bia writes itself onto the disk from memory and waits in land mode with that secret (a few minutes; TCP 4791 must be open in the provider's firewall). 5) carry_fly(host=<address>, timeout_secs=1800) (the saved secret is used; port goes in port=, or host=<address>:<port>): it keeps trying until the server listens. No code is shown; both sides prove the secret and the backup travels encrypted. Afterwards that server runs a copy of this agent and this machine keeps running too; the server deletes its land secret once the agent has landed.
examples: root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|update bia from the internet -> carry_update(from='internet')
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|back up this computer -> discover(path='mcp/carry', enable=true); carry_fold()
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|wait here for another computer to send its settings -> carry_land()
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|send this computer to the one that is waiting -> carry_discover(); carry_fly()
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|the code on both screens is 482193 -> carry_confirm(code='482193')
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|this boot is the flash; become the agent on /dev/sda2 -> carry_morph(disk='/dev/sda2')
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|this flash is newer; fix the internal disk from here -> bash lsblk -f; carry_rescue()
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|install onto the Samsung disk beside Windows on sda5 -> bash lsblk; carry_to_disk(disk='/dev/sda', partition='/dev/sda5')
root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|copy this computer onto the USB stick /dev/sdb -> carry_to_flash(disk='/dev/sdb')

root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|set up my VPS 203.0.113.7 (ssh key in ~/.ssh) as a land and fly there -> carry_new_land_secret(host='203.0.113.7'); bash ssh root@203.0.113.7 'findmnt -no SOURCE /; lsblk -d'; bash ssh root@203.0.113.7 "curl -fsSL …/takeover.sh | bash -s -- --land --land-secret <secret> --yes --wipe /dev/vda --reboot"; carry_fly(host='203.0.113.7', timeout_secs=1800)

root|console|<issued>|<delivered>|the server 198.51.100.9 waits in land mode, its secret is in land-198.51.100.9 -> secrets_get(name='land-198.51.100.9'); carry_fly(host='198.51.100.9', secret='<secret>')
